full_description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

Description

Data Scientist in the HITI Lab (Radiology & Imaging Sciences) responsible for designing and implementing clinical imaging data pipelines, building multimodal AI systems for breast cancer detection and risk assessment, validating commercial clinical AI performance, and contributing to NIH-funded research publications. Position is externally funded through active research grants.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

  • Data Scientist is responsible for mining and analyzing data from various internal and external data sources to drive optimization and improvement of operations, clinical outcomes, and business strategies.
  • Works with stakeholders throughout the organization to drive business solutions and are adept at using large data sets and models to test the effectiveness of different courses of action using predictive algorithms.
  • They assess the effectiveness and accuracy of new data sources and data gathering techniques. Data Scientist is an expert in at least 1 programming language (e.g. R, SAS, Python), has proficiency in statistical theory and underlying mathematical distributions, and expertise in querying relational databases with SQL.
  • They have experience with of a variety of machine learning techniques (clustering, decision tree learning, artificial neural networks, etc.) and can demonstrate real-world application of these techniques.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master's or PhD in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science or another quantitative field and 3 years of relevant experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master’s degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Informatics, Data Science, or related field; 2+ years of data science experience in a research or clinical setting; experience with medical imaging data (DICOM, PACS) and AI/ML model development preferred; proficiency in Python, SQL; strong publication or research record a plus

Additional Details

Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law. Emory University does not discriminate in admissions, educational programs, or employment, including recruitment, hiring, promotions, transfers, discipline, terminations, wage and salary administration, benefits, and training. Students, faculty, and staff are assured of participation in university programs and in the use of facilities without such discrimination. Emory University complies with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Era Veteran's Readjustment Assistance Act, and applicable executive orders, federal and state regulations regarding nondiscrimination, equal opportunity, and affirmative action (for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities). Inquiries regarding this policy should be directed to the Emory University Department of Equity and Civil Rights Compliance, 201 Dowman Drive, Administration Building, Atlanta, GA 30322. Telephone: 404-727-9867 (V) | 404-712-2049 (TDD). Emory University is committed to ensuring equal access and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. To request this document in an alternate format or to seek a reasonable accommodation, please contact the Department of Accessibility Services at accessibility@emory.edu or call 404-727-9877 (Voice) | 404-712-2049 (TDD). We kindly ask that requests be made at least seven business days in advance to allow adequate time for coordination.

Posting Details Position Details Title Prevention Insights: Assistant Research Scientist Appointment Status Non-Tenure Track Department IU Bloomington Applied Health Science Location Bloomington Position Summary The Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington invites applications for an Assistant Research Scientist position at Prevention Insights. We are seeking an Assistant Research Scientist to work with faculty and staff members at Prevention Insights on a variety of externally funded projects, with a primary appointment to support evaluation services. The candidate who is selected will work with Prevention Insights Executive Director Jon Agley, Research Associate Cris Henderson, and other faculty and staff members at Prevention Insights along with external partners from a variety of organizations and agencies. The term of appointment is one year, with potential for renewal on an annual basis by mutual agreement. The candidate may start as early as January 2026. Applications received by November 20, 2026, will receive full consideration. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. This is a hybrid position, meaning that work will be a combination of in-office (Bloomington, IN), remote, and on-site in nearby Indiana counties, as necessary for project success; the specific proportions thereof will largely be determined by project needs and will likely vary over time. Basic Qualifications · Required: Doctoral degree in a subject related or adjacent to public health (e.g., health behavior, psychology, public health nursing, social work, health communication, etc.) or in a methodology commonly used in public health research and evaluation (e.g., biostatistics, qualitative analysis). · Required: Demonstrated ability to work independently and to successfully complete multi-stage projects with limited day-to-day oversight. · Required: Ability to work with both academic and non-academic partners, including other researchers and evaluators, representatives of healthcare organizations and businesses, funders, and community members. · Preference Given For: At least two years of experience in a professional or academic workplace following completion of the terminal degree. · Preference Given For: Experience with one or more software packages that can plausibly assist with research and evaluation (e.g., R, SAS , SPSS , Python). · Preference Given For: Experience with writing grant proposals to federal, state, foundation, or other funders. Responsibilities: · The candidate’s primary responsibility will be to work with an evaluation team at Prevention Insights to assess and support improvement of Indiana’s rural health transformation project in multiple counties. o The candidate will be assigned to lead specific sub-projects that align with their expertise (e.g., leaning toward more quantitative or qualitative work). o The candidate will also be expected to support completion of other sub-projects that they are not directly leading. o This work will involve both internal and public-facing meetings that will be held both virtually and in person (meetings held outside of Bloomington, IN will be eligible for mileage reimbursement at the approved state rate if the candidate transports themself). o The work will be expected to be conducted with a high level of rigor, including an emphasis on accuracy, reproducibility, and transparency. · The candidate will be expected to adhere to standard Prevention Insights- and Indiana University-specific requirements, such as attending staff meetings, completing required annual reporting (e.g., through the university’s performance management tool, currently “Elements”), and maintaining up-to-date training (e.g., CITI , data security). · Since Prevention Insights is a grant- and revenue-funded center, the candidate will be asked to participate in other center-supporting activities from time to time. This may include grant writing, light service on a taskforce (e.g., to accomplish a specific goal at the center), or other work. · The candidate will be expected to develop a degree of independence when it comes to project-specific decision making. They will be expected to proactively identify problems and seek and administer solutions. About Us: Originally founded in 1987 as the Indiana Prevention Resource Center ( IPRC ), Prevention Insights works to help agencies and organizational partners adapt research into practice to deliver robust, evidence-based services in Indiana and beyond. Our work has been supported by local, state, and federal governmental agencies, nonprofit foundations, healthcare organizations, schools, and other organizations. Prevention Insights is a center in the Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington at Indiana University (IU) in Bloomington, Indiana. IU is classified as an R1-Highest Research Activity university, is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities ( AAU ) and boasts numerous resources. Salary : Baseline starting at $70,000, with a higher starting amount negotiable commensurate with experience. Department Contact for Questions Questions pertaining to the PeopleAdmin application procedure may be directed to dwarcher@iu.edu or via postal mail at APHS Postdoc Search & Screen Committee, School Public Health-Bloomington, Indiana University, 1025 East 7th Street, Room 115A, Bloomington, IN 47405-4801. Questions regarding the positions may be directed to Jon Agley ( jagley@iu.edu ). Additional Qualifications Other Notes About the Position: While the successful candidate will have the opportunity to pursue more “traditional” academic products such as peer-reviewed manuscripts and conference presentations, the majority of work output anticipated from this position will be evaluation reports (both internally directed and public-facing) and quality improvement work. Applicants should carefully consider whether this aligns with their desired career trajectory before applying. Salary and Rank Commensurate with Experience Special Instructions Application Procedure: Provide a CV, a cover letter summarizing your fit for the position, up to two examples of your work products that you believe highlight skills related to the position, and a list of three references. Interested candidates should submit applications at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34925 .
